IBKR_ADAPTER_VERIFIED_LIVE.theBugThatOnlyALiveGatewayCouldFind: parseErrorEvent read @stoqey/ib error events backwards. The library always emits (Error, code, reqId); the adapter treated a leading Error argument as proof of a socket failure, so EVERY message classified as socket with code -1, isFatal short-circuited, and isNonFatalError was unreachable dead code. Error 10167, which means delayed data is on its way, therefore killed every price request. It survived because the test mock emitted (reqId, code, message) -- arguments backwards and types wrong -- so 27 green tests certified the bug. Fixed, mock corrected, three tests added pinning the real shape.

ANALYST_PIVOT_2026_09_18: Owner redirected the project on 2026-09-18: stop searching for a mechanical strategy, give the agent discretion over positions from indicators, news and price action. Rationale and constraints in docs/ANALYST-DESIGN.md. THE LOAD-BEARING FACT: this cannot be backtested. A model asked what it would do on a historical date already knows what happened -- market history is in the weights, no holdout split removes it, and the contamination flatters the agent exactly where the pull to deploy is strongest. Forward paper trading is therefore the measurement instrument, not a safety ritual. BUILT SO FAR: analyst/risk.mjs (deterministic veto layer, 32 tests, pure and synchronous, no model inside it), analyst/journal.mjs (append-only decisions with the matched random control drawn AT DECISION TIME from the same eligible pool, 23 tests), analyst/context.mjs (point-in-time by construction plus contextIsPointInTime to test the claim, 16 tests). analyst/decide.mjs is now BUILT (27 tests): one batched call over the cross-section, client injected so every path is drivable by a fake. Model output is treated as UNTRUSTED INPUT -- hallucinated tickers, percent-shaped sizes, oversized positions, missing theses and duplicates are DROPPED AND COUNTED, never repaired, because a repaired proposal is a trade nobody proposed. A max_tokens response is discarded WHOLE rather than partially parsed: a fragment of a plan is a different and unbalanced book, not a smaller one. Text is gathered from all text blocks rather than content[0], since thinking and tool_use blocks also live in content. The test fake was shaped from node_modules @anthropic-ai/sdk messages.d.ts rather than memory, and a standing test asserts field-by-field that it has not drifted -- that test exists because brokers/ibkr.test.mjs once drifted from @stoqey/ib and 27 green tests certified a broken adapter for weeks. THE LOOP AND CLI ARE NOW BUILT (17 more tests; suite 1144/1084/0). analyst/loop.mjs runs ONE batch per call -- no scheduler, no while(true), because a loop owning its own clock cannot be tested or stopped from outside. analyst-run.mjs gives dry-run / paper / score. THE MODE GUARD IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART: paper mode THROWS on a historical date rather than warning, because the failure it prevents is silent and flattering -- nobody sets out to fake a track record, they run the loop over last year to check it works, the numbers look good, and months later those numbers are the reason to go live. scoreJournal scores ONE MODE AT A TIME and reports contaminatedRecords so an exclusion is never silent. VERIFIED END TO END on the real bundle with a stub client: 127 symbols after screening, PARA excluded, context -> decide -> gate -> journal -> outcomes with the matched control all working. THREE REAL BUGS CAUGHT WHILE BUILDING IT. (1) instrumentsFromContext took bars[bars.length-1], the last bar of the WHOLE PANEL rather than the bar at the decision -- a future price sizing a position, which would not throw and would not look wrong in the journal. (2) Quote age was measured against wall-clock in every mode, so every historical dry run died on staleness and the plumbing check degenerated into a test that the staleness rule exists; it now measures against the decision moment, which is identical in paper mode and so still catches a genuinely stale live feed. (3) The CLI checked for an API key before checking panel freshness, so a user would conclude paper mode merely needed credentials when the real blocker was 16-day-old data. NOTE ON THE STUB DRY RUN: its mechanical top-of-slate picks LOST to their own matched control, -0.93% against +0.98%. That is not a finding, it is three names on one date from a non-analyst, and it is recorded only to show the comparison machinery reports honestly against the thing that built it. TWO BUGS CAUGHT WHILE BUILDING CONTEXT, both real: factors.mjs signals take (closes, i, ctx) and volumeTrend reads ctx.volume[symbol], which I was not passing; and per-symbol arrays of different lengths make the same index mean different dates, so the cross-section was not comparable across names. Both fixed by aligning every symbol onto one forward-filled grid the way testSignal does.
ANALYST_NEWS_2026_09_19: analyst/news.mjs and scripts/ibkr-news-probe.mjs built 2026-09-19 (20 tests). This is the last unbuilt piece of the owner's original vision, written BEFORE the Gateway is reachable and deliberately so: the adapter is the cheap part, and writing it now means a route appearing turns into one command rather than an hour. WHY IBKR OVER A NEWS API, restated because it is substantive and not convenience: free news tiers give PUBLICATION time, not AVAILABILITY time. An article stamped 09:31 may have reached the vendor at 14:00, and many are silently revised after publication. Feeding those into a decision log imports a lookahead bug that looks exactly like alpha -- the agent appears to react before the market did because the clock is wrong, not because it was fast. Broker headlines carry the time the broker released them, on the same connection that would place the order. THAT DOES NOT MAKE THEM SAFE. assertNotAfter drops anything at or after the decision boundary and COUNTS it, so a provider systematically stamping wrong shows up as a number rather than as an agent that mysteriously does well on certain days. context.mjs filters news too; the duplication is deliberate belt-and-braces applied at the source as well as at the consumer. A TRAP WORTH RECORDING: the @stoqey/ib newsProviders event delivers ONLY the provider array, with NO reqId, unlike every other news event in that library. Anything written from memory would have added one and then silently never matched. All four signatures were read out of the installed api.d.ts and a standing drift test asserts they still match -- the same guard decide.test.mjs has against the Anthropic SDK. An unparseable headline timestamp is DROPPED, never stamped with now: guessing a time on a decision input is how a 1970 date or a future date slips in unnoticed. Article bodies are fetchable but deliberately NOT wired into the context. Three full articles across forty names would be mostly article, and the model would attend to whichever came first rather than to the cross-section. Headlines go to the analyst; bodies exist so a human reviewing a thesis afterwards can read what the agent was reacting to. RUN 2026-09-19 ON THE OWNER'S MACHINE: three providers entitled (BRFG, BRFUPDN, DJNL), AAPL sample returned 10 headlines. The adapter is verified against the real library. See IBKR_ENTITLEMENTS_MEASURED_2026_09_19. WIRED 2026-09-19 via a cache file (data/news-cache.json, gitignored): news.mjs was BUILT BUT ORPHANED -- nothing in the running system could reach it, so news would still have been missing the moment a Gateway appeared. A cache rather than a live fetch inside the loop, for one decisive reason among three: fetching live would hand a REPLAY today's news for yesterday's decision, which is the exact contamination this design exists to prevent arriving through the back door of a convenience. The cache is a point-in-time record; the other two reasons are that fetching needs a Gateway while deciding does not, and that historical news costs a contract-details round trip plus a news request PER SYMBOL, which would make decision latency a function of TWS pacing limits. VERIFIED END TO END with a synthetic cache carrying one legitimate headline and two dated AFTER the decision: both contaminated ones were dropped and counted (INTCx1, RUNx1) and the legitimate one reached the context attached to INTC. Filtering happens twice, in analyst-run and again in context.mjs, deliberately -- a provider stamping articles forward is the failure that would look most like skill.
NO_TUNNEL_POSSIBLE_2026_09_19: MEASURED 2026-09-19, and it closes off a whole class of proposed fixes. The container CAN run a VPN technically -- /dev/net/tun exists, uid 0, CAP_NET_ADMIN is in the bounding set -- but login.tailscale.com answers 403 at CONNECT. Every tunnel product (Tailscale, ngrok, cloudflared) must reach its own coordination server over the open internet to authenticate, and that is exactly what the proxy denies. So NO TUNNEL CAN BE ESTABLISHED FROM THIS SIDE, and any future plan of the form 'just set up a tunnel' is already answered. Private ranges do bypass the proxy, so a route would work IF one existed -- but nothing can create one from here. THE ANSWER IS THEREFORE TO COLLECT WHERE THE GATEWAY ALREADY IS. scripts/ibkr-collect.mjs does all three probes in one invocation (news entitlement + sample, sector map, intraday ladder) and writes data/ files to be committed and picked up here. It depends on @stoqey/ib and NOTHING else: the repo's package.json also carries canvas, which needs a native toolchain and would turn a one-command job into an afternoon, so every other import in the chain is a node builtin or a dependency-free local module. USE THE PAPER GATEWAY (4002, or 7497 for TWS). Everything collected is read-only and available on paper. ONE CAVEAT recorded so it is not mistaken for a result later: a standalone paper account may not inherit the live account's market-data subscriptions, so ZERO news providers on paper is not conclusive -- re-check against live before concluding news is unavailable.
IBKR_ENTITLEMENTS_MEASURED_2026_09_19: The three open entitlement questions were answered by running scripts/ibkr-collect.mjs on the OWNER'S machine against a paper Gateway (127.0.0.1:4002, Read-Only API on), 2026-09-19T21:58Z. This is the first time any of the analyst's IBKR code has touched a real Gateway. Read-only throughout: reqNewsProviders, reqContractDetails, reqHistoricalNews, reqHistoricalData. No order path exists in that script or anything it imports. NEWS: ENTITLED, THREE PROVIDERS, FREE TIER. BRFG (Briefing.com General Market Columns), BRFUPDN (Briefing.com Analyst Actions), DJNL (Dow Jones Newsletters). A sample reqHistoricalNews for AAPL returned 10 headlines. The whole path therefore works end to end against the real library, not against a mock: provider listing, conId resolution, headline fetch, timestamp parse, cache write. The newsProviders-has-no-reqId trap recorded in ANALYST_NEWS_2026_09_19 was read correctly -- had it been wrong the provider list would have hung and returned empty, which is exactly what a missing entitlement also looks like. The earlier caveat (that zero providers on a standalone paper account would not be conclusive and would need re-checking against live) is MOOT: the answer was not zero. WHAT THE THREE PROVIDERS ARE AND ARE NOT. They are the free bundle every IBKR account carries. They are not Reuters, Dow Jones real-time newswire, or Benzinga -- those are paid adds. BRFUPDN in particular is analyst upgrades and downgrades, which is the single most decision-relevant free feed here and is the reason the news slot is worth having at all. PREDICTION MADE HERE AND LATER FALSIFIED, left visible rather than edited away: I wrote that the free bundle would give thin per-symbol coverage on the mid-cap tail. It does not. Measured 2026-09-21 on this universe: 114 of 118 symbols carry headlines, 96.6%. The prediction was wrong and the reasoning behind it (an editor chooses what to cover, so coverage will be patchy) was a plausible story rather than a measurement. NOTE THE UNIVERSE THOUGH -- these are S&P 500 constituents, which is the easy case. The claim is untested on the genuine small caps in universe/candidates.txt and must be re-measured there rather than either repeated or abandoned. WHAT SURVIVES INTACT: absence of a headline is still not evidence of an uneventful day, because it remains an editorial decision rather than a market fact, and the analyst must not read silence as calm. SECTORS: 118 of 128 symbols classified into 8 groups, 0 ambiguous, 10 unclassified and left out rather than bucketed. Scheme is IBKR-industry -- IBKR's own taxonomy, recorded as such and NOT crosswalked to GICS. This unblocks MR04 and the other sector-dependent Tier B items. Note 8 groups, not the 11 GICS sectors; the partition is coarser, which weakens MR04's test somewhat and should be said in the verdict rather than discovered later. INTRADAY: all six legitimate rungs SUCCEEDED. 1 D/1 min -> 390 bars (a full RTH session, exactly right), 2 D/1 min -> 780, 5 D/5 mins -> 390, 1 M/30 mins -> 273, 6 M/1 hour -> 875, 1 Y/1 day -> 251. The bar counts are internally coherent, so this is real data and not a truncated or padded response. INTRADAY HISTORY IS A PULL, NOT A PURCHASE. A PRECISION POINT ON THE OVER-ASK RUNG, because reading it loosely would overstate the result. 1 Y of 1-min bars came back ok:false with reason 'timeout' -- NOT an explicit entitlement refusal. A timeout is ambiguous: it is consistent with a refusal the client never surfaced, with TWS pacing, and with the server simply taking longer than 15s to assemble ~98000 bars. So the ladder does NOT cleanly establish an upper boundary. What it DOES establish is the lower one, which is the part that mattered: minute bars are retrievable. Do not cite the last row as evidence of a limit. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SOLVE. The container still cannot route to the Gateway (NO_TUNNEL_POSSIBLE_2026_09_19 stands). Every one of these pulls happened on the owner's machine and arrived here as committed files. So a refreshed price panel -- the actual blocker on forward paper trading, the bundle's last bar being 2026-09-03 -- is a MANUAL step on the owner's side, not something the agent can do on a schedule. Any claim that paper mode is 'ready' has to name who runs the refresh and how often.
MR04_VOID_AND_THE_ETF_FINDING_2026_09_19: MR04 ran for the first time on 2026-09-19 against the owner's real IBKR sector map and came back VOID. Cell C, the pre-registered market-only reproduction check, returned +28.45% net / Sharpe 0.724 against a written-down expectation of +49.25% / 0.963 with a 20-point tolerance. The runner scored nothing and repaired nothing, which is what the pre-registration told it to do. THE PRE-REGISTRATION'S INFERENCE RULE WAS WRONG. It said a gap of tens of points means the runner is wrong. It is not: handed a map covering all 127 screened names the same runner returns +49.21% / 0.962, and a separately written diagnostic reproduces +49.25% / 0.963 exactly. The registration enumerated two explanations and the truth was a third. WHAT IBKR REFUSED TO CLASSIFY. 10 of the 127 names have no industry field because they are not companies: IWM, QQQ, SPY, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLU, XLV. sector-map.mjs dropped them rather than bucketing them, which is what it was built for, and the Utilities sector went too at 2 members. Every step of the data is correct; the study's assumption about what was in its universe was not. Nothing in this repository had recorded that the bundle is 117 stocks plus 10 ETFs. A FIRST EXPLANATION WAS PUBLISHED AND THEN REFUTED, AND THAT SEQUENCE IS THE POINT. The first write-up of this said the move was the ranking pool alone and that the ETFs constituted a different mechanism -- a cap-weight-versus-equal-weight spread -- so that roughly half of RESIDUAL-MEAN-REVERSION's headline cell was that spread. It was plausible and it was wrong, and it was wrong because I reasoned about the mechanism instead of measuring it. Three measurements killed it. Selection frequency: ETFs are 7.8% of the long leg's 2067 picks against a 7.9% pool share, so the book did not prefer them. Return: ETF picks earn 0.405% mean gross forward return against stock picks' 0.408%, a difference of three thousandths of a percent. Score distribution: ETF residual z has mean -0.058 sd 1.294 against stocks' -0.013 sd 1.327. On every axis that would show a different mechanism, they are indistinguishable from the stocks. WHAT ACTUALLY DIFFERS IS VARIANCE, AND IT IS A GEOMETRY EFFECT. ETF picks have per-pick sd 2.25% against the stocks' 5.85%, 2.6x lower, which is what a basket of 100+ names is for. Ten low-variance instruments available to a 13-name leg damp the leg's dispersion. That raises Sharpe mechanically and raises COMPOUNDED return through reduced volatility drag at an unchanged arithmetic mean. It is the same lesson RESIDUAL-MEAN-REVERSION already recorded -- the Sharpe belongs to the geometry, not the signal -- reached independently by a second route. THE DECOMPOSITION, ONE CHANGE AT A TIME FROM THE +49.25% ANCESTOR. These are one-at-a-time effects with interactions and do NOT sum to the total: leg size 13 -> 12 alone costs 7.65 points (49.25 -> 41.60); dropping the 10 ETFs from the ranking pool alone at 13/leg costs 10.21 (49.25 -> 39.04); both together give 29.36; the 2 Utilities names cost a further 2.96; changing the FACTOR set from 127 to stocks GAINS 2.05. MORE THAN A THIRD OF THE MOVE IS ONE NAME IN THE LEG. A headline that swings 7.65 points on 13 versus 12 names is not a robust quantity, and the original study's k-window instability was the same fragility seen from another angle. MR04 IS VOID, NOT CLOSED. Its claim -- that sector-neutralising the residual adds something the market-only residual missed -- was never tested, because the run stopped at the control. Re-running needs an AMENDED pre-registration that separates the factor-estimation set from the ranking set, fixes leg size explicitly rather than letting it fall out of pool size, and does NOT carry over C_EXPECTED_NET. Writing that amendment after seeing these numbers is a real hazard and must be labelled as an amendment with its reasoning stated independently of the result. Not written yet; no amended run made.
NULL_CALIBRATION_RECHECKED_2026_09_19: The calibration is the most-reused number in this project: a random-selection null returning ~+33.70% net at mean Sharpe ~0.85, which five closed studies cite as the bar gate 2 uses. Both independent replications drew from the 127-name pool, so once the pool was found to contain 10 ETFs the number needed rechecking rather than reusing. null-calibration.mjs does it at 2000 draws on three pools, inheriting the geometry and the residual study's seed. It scores no strategy and has no cells; it recomputes two reference quantities. IT SURVIVES. Pool A (127 names, 13/leg) reproduces +33.70% net / Sharpe 0.850 long-only and -29.43% long-short -- both recorded figures to the digit, which is also a clean independent reproduction of the residual study's null machinery. On stocks alone (117, 12/leg): +34.28% / 0.826 and -29.71%. Holding leg size at 13 to isolate composition: +33.99% / 0.832. The gate-1 baseline moves from +68.86% to +67.97%. EVERY SHIFT IS INSIDE A FRACTION OF THE NULL'S OWN 5-95% SPREAD, roughly [0%, 73%] for the long-only book. No closed verdict is affected and the calibration may be quoted as before, with the pool named. This is a negative result on my own concern and is recorded as fully as a positive one would be. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE INFORMATIVE PART. A RANDOM book is nearly indifferent to leg size: 33.99% at 13/leg against 34.28% at 12/leg, a third of a point. The RESIDUAL book swings 7.65 points on the identical change. A signal book that much more sensitive than its own null to a one-name perturbation has its return concentrated in a few picks at the decile boundary. That is fragility, not edge, and it is worth carrying into how the analyst's book is sized.
BUNDLE_IS_SPLIT_ADJUSTED_2026_09_19: sp500-bundle's adjustment basis had never been checked, and it decides whether IBKR bars can be appended to it. Scanned all 128 series for split-shaped discontinuities: a close-to-close jump near a simple ratio (2,3,4,5,...,30) in either direction. THREE HITS, ALL UPWARD, SO NONE IS A SPLIT. LUMN 2024-08-06 +93% on 7x volume; PARA 2024-09-20 +98% on 101x volume and 2024-09-24 +96% on 40x. A split moves price DOWN and share volume up proportionally; none of these has that shape, and PARA is the corrupted series screenUniverse already rejects for a 107,453x close range. THE BUNDLE IS SPLIT-ADJUSTED. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, AND IT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. Split-adjusted does not mean dividend-adjusted, and the dividend question cannot be answered offline. Dividend adjustment is applied BACKWARDS from the present, so a dividend-adjusted series' most recent bars are nearly raw -- an overlap check across the 16-day gap would MATCH while three years of older history sat on a different basis. The discriminating test is cross-sectional: ratio-to-IBKR should scale with dividend yield, deviating on KO and XOM and not on zero-dividend names. It needs a Gateway and has not been run. CONSEQUENCE: scripts/ibkr-panel.mjs writes a SEPARATE ROOT (ibkr-bundle/) and never appends to sp500-bundle. An unverifiable join is not made, and sixteen closed verdicts were computed on sp500-bundle exactly as it stands.
PANEL_FRESHNESS_IS_SESSION_COUNTED_2026_: The paper-mode staleness guard counted wall-clock hours (36h in loop.mjs, 1.5 days in analyst-run.mjs). Under forward-only measurement that guard is the measurement instrument, not a nicety, and the wall-clock form was wrong in the most ordinary case: it refused every Monday holding Friday's bar, and every day after a holiday. A correct panel reading as a broken feed is how an operator learns to ignore the guard. REPLACED WITH SESSION COUNTING DERIVED FROM THE PANEL ITSELF. sessionWeekdays() reads which weekdays the panel actually trades rather than assuming Monday-to-Friday -- discipline rule 4, and a hardcoded five-day week is silently wrong for crypto. missedSessions() counts trading weekdays strictly after the last bar up to now. More than one missed session refuses. THE ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE. A holiday the panel has not seen yet counts as a missed session, making the check too STRICT by one day. That fails safe: it refuses to trade. The opposite error -- a tolerance wide enough to span a long holiday weekend -- would let a genuinely stale mid-week panel through, and that produces contaminated evidence that looks like a track record. Five tests pin both directions.
NEWS_ENVELOPE_2026_09_19: The first real headlines exposed a defect only real data could show. IBKR wraps every headline in a metadata envelope: `{A:800015:L:en}Apple Bites Into Record Q3...`, and on three of the ten collected, `{A:800015:L:en:K:n/a:C:0.9775911569595337}!Rosenblatt reiterated...`. news.mjs was passing that straight through, so the analyst would have read roughly forty tokens of vendor bookkeeping at the front of every headline, inside a context that is explicitly a budget. No mock had caught it because no mock emitted it -- rule 6 again, from the other direction: the mock was faithful to the SIGNATURE and not to the PAYLOAD. parseHeadlineText splits the envelope off, strips a leading `!` (it appears on BRFUPDN analyst-action headlines and not on BRFG prose ones, so it is a provider marker and providerCode already carries that in usable form), and returns the text, the parsed fields and the original. An unrecognised shape is returned UNCHANGED rather than guessed at, so a provider that stops sending the envelope does not have its first characters eaten. toNewsMap falls back through the parser for caches written before this, so an old cache cannot leak braces. THE C FIELD IS PARSED AND DELIBERATELY NOT INTERPRETED. It looks like a relevance or confidence score and surfacing it as one would be easy. Three samples, all above 0.77, is not a basis for telling an analyst what a number means, and a misread score is worse than none because it arrives wearing the vendor's authority. It is carried under `meta` as a string for a later probe to settle against a larger sample or IBKR's own documentation. A test asserts nothing consumes it. This is an OPEN QUESTION, not a decision.
UNFINISHED_HOLDS_2026_09_20: Found by verifying the day's own changes rather than by a test: a dry run at the end of the panel returned three different names AND the matched random control all at exactly -0.11%. Identical figures across four independent series is not a result, and -0.11% is exactly the round trip (2 x (0.005% fee + 0.05% slip)) charged on a gross return of zero. CAUSE: forwardReturn clamped the exit index to the last available bar, so an entry ON the last bar exited on the same bar, returned 0, and presented as a completed flat trade. It never threw and never looked wrong in isolation -- only the coincidence of four identical numbers exposed it. WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN A DRY-RUN COSMETIC. realisedOutcomes is documented as producing rows ready for recordOutcome, and paper scoring NECESSARILY runs while the newest decisions are still inside their holding period. Every such decision would have been written to the journal as a completed 0% trade. That packs the track record with fabricated zeroes, drags the measured edge toward nothing, and makes the agent look CONSISTENT while doing it -- contaminating the single instrument this design has for knowing whether it works. FIX: forwardReturn now returns the realised return AND the number of sessions actually available. realisedOutcomes drops incomplete holds by default (rule 8, drop and count, never repair) and carries sessionsHeld and complete on every row. The CLI passes requireComplete:false so a human reading a dry run sees 'INCOMPLETE - 0/5 sessions available' instead of an empty section, while any journal writer gets the dropping default. Three tests pin end-of-panel, partial, and completed holds.
SETTLEMENT_LOOP_CLOSED_2026_09_20: Found the same way as the unfinished-hold bug: by running the paths rather than trusting the suite. `analyst-run.mjs score` was exercised end to end for the first time and reported `outcomes 0` on a journal holding four decision batches. The cause is not a bug in scoring -- NOTHING IN THE SYSTEM EVER CALLED recordOutcome. Decisions were journalled, realisedOutcomes could compute results, and the two were never connected, so score could only ever print dashes however long the agent ran. A measurement instrument that cannot record a measurement is not one, and this is the instrument the whole no-backtest argument rests on. A SECOND GAP UNDERNEATH IT: the decision record did not store which bar the decision was made on. The only route back was parsing the date out of batchId, and a derived string is not a schema. recordDecision now stores asOfTime, taken from the context. buildContext exposes it as an epoch alongside the formatted asOf. AND THE ANONYMISATION TRAP THAT CAME WITH IT. anonymiseContext spreads the named context and nulls the date fields; adding a raw epoch would have sailed straight through and undone the anonymisation, which exists so an anonymised probe cannot let the model recall what happened on a known date. asOfTime is nulled there too and a test asserts the epoch appears nowhere in the serialised anonymised context. settleOutcomes() in loop.mjs computes and appends outcomes for every decision whose holding period has finished, and analyst-run.mjs gains a `settle` subcommand. SEPARATE FROM THE DECISION because the holding period has not elapsed when the decision is made -- settlement happens days later on a later run, which is exactly why it must be IDEMPOTENT: the journal is append-only, so a duplicate outcome cannot be taken back and would be double-counted by every figure scoreJournal produces. Already-settled (batchId, symbol) pairs are skipped and counted. A decision whose entry bar the current panel does not contain is SKIPPED AND COUNTED, never settled against a nearby bar. Guessing an entry price is how a track record stops describing the trades that were actually proposed. Four tests pin idempotency, unfinished holds, unknown entry bars, and mode isolation -- the last because a dry run must never settle into the paper record. VERIFIED END TO END on a scratch journal: 5 dry-run batches, settle wrote 12 outcomes and left 3 inside their holding period, a second settle wrote 0 and reported 12 already settled, and score then read 12 outcomes instead of 0. THE NUMBERS THAT READOUT PRINTS ARE MEANINGLESS -- the client was the stub, which picks mechanically off the top of the slate, and the readout correctly labels the mode NOT EVIDENCE OF EDGE. What was verified is the path, not a result.
ANONYMISED_MODE_WAS_NEVER_FUNCTIONAL_202: THE THIRD DEFECT OF THE SAME CLASS IN THREE TICKS, all found by running paths rather than trusting a green suite. MODE.ANONYMISED is described in docs/ANALYST-DESIGN.md as one of three modes and has unit tests, and NO CLI PATH COULD EVER PRODUCE IT -- `score --mode anonymised` could be asked for, but no subcommand ever set the mode, so an anonymised journal could not exist. Same shape as recordOutcome: built, documented, unreachable. MAKING IT REACHABLE IMMEDIATELY SHOWED IT WAS ALSO BROKEN. The first real run rejected every proposal with `no_usable_price`. instrumentsFromContext was looking up a price series under the name 'Asset A'. The mode could never have produced a single allowed decision, so it could never have probed reasoning, which is the only thing it exists for. THE FIX IS A BOUNDARY, NOT A PATCH. The model must see hashed labels or the mode is pointless; the risk gate must see real instruments or it cannot price anything. The gate is deterministic code, not the model, so it may legitimately know the identities. runOnce now builds the NAMED context, derives instruments and the control pool from it, anonymises a copy for the model call alone, and translates the model's aliases back before the gate. The mapping is positional so it is RECOMPUTED by aliasToSymbol rather than hidden on the anonymised object -- a hidden field would be one JSON.stringify away from leaking every identity the mode exists to remove. A CASE BUG INSIDE THE FIX, worth recording because it failed in the most misleading way available. decide normalises proposed symbols to upper case, so a map keyed on 'Asset A' missed the 'ASSET A' that came back, and every proposal was dropped as an unrecognised label -- which reads exactly like the model inventing labels. Keyed upper case now. VERIFIED BY CAPTURING WHAT THE MODEL ACTUALLY RECEIVED, not by assertion: across the full 127-name panel, zero real tickers and zero date strings appear in the 14,619 bytes sent, while the gate priced and allowed RUN, WBD and INTC. Anonymisation holds and the mode functions. A CORRECTION MADE WITHIN THE SAME TICK: the CLI first announced that anonymised decisions cannot be settled. That was written from the broken behaviour. They now carry real symbols and a decision bar, so they ARE settleable -- and remain NOT evidence of edge, because the anonymisation cannot be proven complete, not because the plumbing is absent. AND ONE DEFENCE TURNED OUT TO BE THE SECOND LINE, NOT THE FIRST: decide already refuses a symbol absent from the context it was given, so an invented alias never reaches the translation step. The test now records WHICH line caught it, so a later change to either is visible rather than silently leaving one.
FRESHNESS_GUARD_CORRECTED_2026_09_20: The session-counting freshness guard written earlier the same day was WRONG, and rehearsing the paper path found it. The guard had only ever been observed REFUSING, because the real panel is weeks stale; nobody had seen it pass. A current-dated copy of the panel was built in the scratchpad (real prices, shifted dates, never committed) purely to walk the path with the guard satisfied. IT PASSED A PANEL IT SHOULD HAVE REFUSED. Sunday 2026-09-20, panel's last bar Thursday 2026-09-17. Friday's session had closed and its bar was absent, and the guard allowed it. The rule was 'more than one missed session refuses', which is the same as 'excuse today' ONLY while today is a trading day. On a Saturday or Sunday it excuses the most recent REAL session instead. CORRECTED RULE: excuse today, and only today, and only when today trades -- its bar may legitimately not exist yet because the session is not over. Every earlier session has closed, so a missing bar for one means a stale panel. The threshold is now zero missed completed sessions. Checked cases: Monday holding Friday passes (0); Wednesday holding Monday refuses (Tuesday closed, 1); Sunday holding Thursday refuses (Friday closed, 1); Sunday holding Friday passes (0). Four tests, one per case. A PROCESS NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX. The first patch attempt silently half-applied: a Python heredoc raised a SyntaxError on the loop.mjs edit while the analyst-run.mjs edit in the following block succeeded, so the CLI enforced the corrected rule and the library still enforced the old one. `node --check` passed on both files because both were valid JavaScript. Caught by grepping for the actual threshold in both files rather than trusting the exit status. A multi-file edit needs verification of the RESULT, not of the tool's report. AND ONE APPARENT FAILURE THAT WAS NOT ONE. A second rehearsal panel shifted by 15 days was expected to pass and refused. The panel was the problem: 15 is not a multiple of 7, so every weekday rotated and sessionWeekdays correctly derived a Tue-Sat trading week, under which Saturday was a genuinely missed session. Verified by printing the derived week rather than assuming. Incidentally this is the clearest demonstration so far that the calendar really is read from the data, which is what discipline rule 4 asks for.
FUTURE_DATED_PANEL_GUARD_2026_09_20: The freshness guard only ever looked BACKWARDS. A panel whose last bar is dated four days from now passed it cleanly -- nothing was missing, so nothing was refused. Measured before fixing: missedSessions returned 0 and the guard said PASS. THIS IS THE WORST FAILURE AVAILABLE TO THIS DESIGN, which is why it is worth a guard of its own rather than a note. The entire architecture exists to stop the model seeing data from after the decision. A future-dated panel means the context is assembled from bars that have not happened, in the ONE mode that counts as evidence, and the run looks clean throughout -- no exception, no warning, and a journal entry indistinguishable from a real one. IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Bar timestamps arrive in the account's timezone and are parsed; a machine clock can be wrong; a vendor can stamp forward. This project had ALREADY written that risk down for news -- 'a provider stamping articles forward is the failure that would look most like skill' -- and then left the price panel unguarded against exactly the same thing. The lesson generalises: a hazard recorded for one input is a hazard to check for every input. sessionsAhead() compares at DAY granularity, because a daily bar is stamped at the start of its session while `now` sits somewhere inside it; comparing instants would call every mid-session bar the future. Paper mode refuses any positive value, and the message says CORRUPT INPUT rather than stale -- calling it staleness would send whoever reads it looking in precisely the wrong direction. Dry run is deliberately NOT blocked: it names its own decision bar, so a panel extending past today is not a contradiction there. Verified at both levels, after last tick's half-applied patch: the threshold was grepped out of both loop.mjs and analyst-run.mjs to confirm they agree, and the CLI was run against a future-dated panel to see the refusal rather than infer it. Three tests, including one asserting the error does NOT say 'sessions behind'.
NEWS_PROVENANCE_AND_COVERAGE_2026_09_20: THE JOURNAL RECORDED NOTHING ABOUT NEWS. Confirmed by dumping a decision record: kind, batchId, at, mode, model, contextHash, asOfTime, proposals, allowed, rejected, exposure, halted, braked, control, poolSize -- and no mention of news at all. So a batch decided on price alone and a batch decided with a full news panel were indistinguishable afterwards. WHY THAT IS NOT COSMETIC. The design argument for the entire pivot, written into docs/ANALYST-DESIGN.md, is that the edge must come from the NON-PRICE input, because the price half is already closed in VERDICTS.md. A track record that cannot separate 'decided with news' from 'decided with none' measures a blend and then credits the mechanism. The one claim this design rests on could not have been tested against its own control population. RECORDED, NOT ENFORCED, and the distinction is the point. Refusing to run without news would have been the wrong fix: an analyst working on price alone is a legitimate analyst and, more importantly, IS the control population the news thesis has to beat. Both populations are needed, so both are kept and labelled. Every decision now carries candidates, candidatesWithNews, headlines, plus the cache's source, fetchedAt, ageHours, stale flag and droppedAtBoundary count. THE FIRST THING IT MEASURED WAS A REAL PROBLEM. Run through the real CLI against the real cache: candidatesWithNews 0 of 40 candidates, headlines 0, droppedAtBoundary 0. Nothing was being filtered out -- the cache simply covers ONE symbol. scripts/ibkr-collect.mjs fetched headlines for AAPL alone as proof the path worked. It did work, and it left the analyst running with news on 0.8% of its universe. A news input covering 1 of 127 names is not a news input, it is a plumbing test left in place. COLLECTOR RESTRUCTURED to four steps so headlines cover the whole universe: entitlement, then sectors, then headlines, then the intraday ladder. News moved AFTER sectors deliberately -- that pass already pays for a reqContractDetails per symbol and historical news needs the conId it returns, so the conIds are captured there and reused. Resolving them twice would have doubled the slowest part of the script for nothing. Paced separately at 600ms because TWS limits historical news harder than contract details, and capped at 8 headlines per symbol because the context is a budget. THE COLLECTOR NOW STATES THE ASYMMETRY OUT LOUD: symbols returning nothing are reported as COVERAGE, not calm. The free Briefing.com bundle covers what its editors chose to write about, so absence of a headline on a mid-cap is not evidence of an uneventful day, and an analyst that reads it as one is reading an editorial decision as a market fact. resolveConId was removed because this change is what made it dead -- own orphans, not pre-existing ones.
NEWS_SPLIT_IN_THE_READOUT_2026_09_20: Last tick added a news-provenance field to every decision record. This tick checked whether anything READ it: nothing did. That is precisely the pattern the previous five ticks were spent fixing -- recordOutcome written and never called, MODE.ANONYMISED documented and unreachable -- reproduced the same day by the fix for it. Writing a field nobody reads is the same defect as building a mode nobody can run. GRANULARITY WAS WRONG TOO, and the coarse version would have been misleading rather than merely useless. The batch summary says how many candidates carried headlines; the claim under test is about the NAME being bought. A batch with news on two of forty candidates would have marked all forty as informed. `hadNews` is therefore recorded per allowed name, computed from the same candidate set the model saw. scoreJournal now splits outcomes into withNews / withoutNews / unknown and reports each arm's mean net, its own control mean, and its edge. THE EDGES ARE THE COMPARISON, NOT THE NETS: each arm carries its own matched random control, and two arms drawn from different slates can differ in mean return for reasons that have nothing to do with news. NO VERDICT IS COMPUTED AND A THRESHOLD SAYS WHEN NOT TO LOOK. `comparable` requires 20+ outcomes in EACH arm, and the readout says NOT YET COMPARABLE below that rather than printing two numbers side by side and inviting the eye to compare them. Splitting a small sample makes two smaller ones, and the payoff distribution the owner is aiming at is skewed, which needs MORE outcomes than a symmetric one, not fewer. ABSENT PROVENANCE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ABSENT NEWS. A decision written before the flag existed records hadNews as null and lands in `unknown`, never in `withoutNews`. Folding unknown into the no-news arm would manufacture a control population out of missing metadata. A test pins it. FIRST READING ON A REAL JOURNAL: 0 outcomes with a headline, 12 without. That is the one-symbol news cache showing up in the evidence layer, exactly as the collector fix last tick predicted it would. The instrument reports the coverage problem rather than averaging over it.
UNIVERSE_CANDIDATES_2026_09_21: universe/candidates.txt: 1,047 unique tickers assembled at the owner's request for the broadest practical coverage. Composition is deliberately cross-sectional rather than index-shaped: mega-cap tech through micro-cap biotech, all eleven sectors, plus sector and broad-market ETFs, international, rates, credit and commodity proxies so the analyst can see a macro backdrop rather than infer one. 120 of the 1,047 are already in sp500-bundle; 927 are new. UNVERIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT IS STATED IN THE FILE ITSELF. The list was assembled from model knowledge, not from a broker, so it certainly contains names acquired, renamed or delisted since the knowledge cutoff. No list built away from the broker can know which. IBKR is the authority: ibkr-panel.mjs reports every symbol it cannot resolve and now WRITES THE RESOLVED ONES to universe-resolved.txt, so the first pull is the cleaning pass and the failures stop repeating. This is the same discipline as the entitlement probes -- measured, not assumed. A PARSER BUG FOUND BEFORE SHIPPING THE FILE, not after. The --symbols reader tokenised on whitespace and accepted any 1-10 letter word, so a heading like '# Semis and memory' contributed SEMIS, AND and MEMORY as tickers. Confirmed by running the parser on a commented sample before writing the list. A universe file is the natural place for a human to write headings, so the format has to survive one; comments are now stripped per line before tokenising. RESUMABILITY ADDED FOR THE SAME REASON THE LIST IS BIG. IBKR paces historical data requests hard (documented at roughly 60 per ten minutes, NOT verified here), so a thousand-name pull runs for hours and will be interrupted. --skip-fresh skips symbols whose CSV already reaches within --fresh-days of current, so re-running continues rather than restarting, and the daily refresh becomes cheap. The pacing figure is quoted from documentation and should be MEASURED on the owner's first large run rather than trusted. THE TENSION THE OWNER SHOULD DECIDE, NOT ME. A 1,047-name universe does not mean the analyst sees 1,047 names. context.mjs shows a slate (default 40: held positions, then top and bottom by rankBy). So the bigger the universe, the MORE the mechanical ranker decides and the LESS the analyst does -- which cuts against the stated reason for this pivot. Measured context cost is ~365 bytes per candidate: slate 40 ~4K tokens, 200 ~18K, 400 ~37K, the whole universe ~96K. A larger slate is affordable; whether it is desirable is a judgment about where the decision should live.
SLATE_SET_TO_300_2026_09_21: The owner set the slate to 300 on 2026-09-21, against the new ~1,000-name candidate universe. Default changed in context.mjs, loop.mjs and analyst-run.mjs. This is a POLICY choice, not a performance knob, and the reasoning is recorded in context.mjs beside the parameter: whatever the universe holds, the analyst only ever sees the slate, so a wide universe behind a narrow slate means the RANKER chooses and the analyst ratifies -- which is the mechanical rule this project pivoted away from. MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED. ~365 bytes per candidate. On the current 127-name universe: slate 40 showed 40 of 127 at 14KB (~4K tokens); slate 300 shows all 127 at 43KB (~11K tokens). Against the 1,047-name universe it will show 300 and omit ~750, at roughly 27K tokens. Held positions are always shown on top of the slate, so the real count can exceed it. A SMALL TRUTHFULNESS BUG FELL OUT OF THE CHANGE. When the slate exceeds the universe the slices simply return the whole cross-section, but the universe note still read 'the top and bottom 150 by momentum' while showing all 127 names. That note exists specifically to tell the analyst the shape of what it is NOT seeing, so telling it about a selection that was never applied invites reasoning about a filter that does not exist. It now says 'the entire cross-section is shown; nothing was ranked away' when that is the case, with a test for both branches. A TEST-SETUP ERROR CAUGHT AND NOT MISREAD AS A CODE BUG: the first version of that test built a 200-bar panel and read asOf 150, which is below the indicator lookback, so nothing was rankable and the slate was empty for reasons unrelated to its width. Sized to match the rest of the file instead of loosening the assertion. STILL OPEN AND STILL THE OWNER'S: at slate 300 against 1,047 names, roughly 750 names in the middle of the ranking are never seen by the analyst in any given batch. That is inherent to a ranked slate, not a defect, but it means the mechanical ranker still decides what is invisible. Worth revisiting once the forward record shows where decisions actually come from.
NEWS_COVERAGE_MEASURED_2026_09_21: The four-step collector ran on the owner's machine 2026-09-21T00:28Z. NEWS COVERAGE IS GOOD, AND BETTER THAN PREDICTED: 114 of 118 symbols carry headlines, 884 headlines total, 0 failed requests, 0 dated in the future. The earlier caution -- that the free Briefing.com bundle would be thin on anything outside the mega-caps -- is NOT what the data shows on an S&P-500-shaped universe. 96.6% coverage. That caution should be re-tested, not repeated, once the 1,047-name universe with its genuine small-caps lands; a list of large caps is the easy case. PACING AT 600ms HELD: 118 historical-news requests, zero failures. The IBKR pacing worry recorded earlier was about reqHistoricalData, not reqHistoricalNews, and news at this rate is fine. The historical-DATA rate still has not been tested at scale and remains the open question for the panel pull. THE PER-SYMBOL CAP IS BINDING: 884 headlines over 114 symbols is 7.75 average against a cap of 8, so most names returned the maximum and more news exists than was pulled. That is a different fact from 'the feed is thin' and leads somewhere different. The collector now counts how many symbols hit the cap and says so, rather than leaving it to be inferred from an average. A REAL BUG THE REPORT EXPOSED, in code written the previous tick. The news pass covered 118 symbols -- exactly the CLASSIFIED count, not the 128 collected. conIds were captured after the classification `continue`s, so any name that resolved fine but carried no industry label got no conId and therefore no news. That silently excluded every ETF: SPY, QQQ and the seven XL* sector funds. They are not companies so they have no industry; they emphatically do have news, and market-level commentary is precisely the macro backdrop an analyst cannot infer from price. 'Can I identify this instrument' and 'does it have a sector' are different questions and must not share a branch. Fixed by capturing the conId immediately after details resolve. NOT YET PUSHED as of this entry: the owner ran the collector but the data (news-cache.json with 884 headlines, sector-map.json) is still only on their machine. The committed data/ remains the 2026-09-19 one-symbol cache.
PAPER_RUN_PREREGISTERED_2026_09_24: The owner stated the plan: about a month of paper, roughly 20 trading days, then a decision about live money. docs/PAPER-PROTOCOL.md pre-registers what that month is a test OF, committed before any paper decision exists. The timing is the method: once a track record exists it is too late to ask what would count as success, because whatever happened becomes the thing defended. THE ARITHMETIC, MEASURED OFF THE PANEL BY paper-power.mjs RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The independent unit is the non-overlapping holding period, NOT the trade. Twenty trading days of daily decisions on a five-day hold looks like a hundred trades and is FOUR independent observations -- holds overlap, every name in a batch shares one market, and one bad week contaminates every decision inside it. Counting trades overstates the evidence by roughly an order of magnitude in the flattering direction. Simulating the null by drawing two random books per period from the real panel (20,000 draws, book of 10): 20 trading days = 4 periods resolves only an edge of 3.4% per period, about 170% annualised. 60 days = 12 periods, ~98% annualised. Six months = 26 periods, ~67%. One year = 50 periods, ~48%. A MONTH CAN ONLY DETECT AN EDGE SO LARGE THAT SEEING IT SHOULD PROMPT SUSPICION OF THE MEASUREMENT. Even a full year only resolves edges near 48% annualised, which is far above any real one. A LEVER TESTED AND CLOSED. Shortening the hold looks like it buys sample size: one-day holds give 20 periods in a month instead of 4. Derived first, then measured across holds of 1, 2, 5, 10 and 21 days -- the annualised detectable edge stays between 157% and 181% at every hold, because per-period noise falls with the square root of the hold while period count rises linearly and the two cancel. What does not cancel is cost: drag rises from 1.32%/yr at 21-day holds to 27.72%/yr at one-day holds. Shorter holds slice the same evidence thinner and pay more for it. THE CONSEQUENCE, WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE ANY NUMBER EXISTS: no practical paper period will prove edge. The decision to risk real money will therefore rest on something other than statistical proof. That is not an argument against making it; it is an argument for making it consciously. A sign-off can honestly mean 'ran clean for a month, risk envelope held, reasoning reviewable, owner chose to risk capital on an unproven edge with a known downside'. It cannot honestly mean 'the numbers proved it'. WHAT THE MONTH CAN ANSWER is operational and is pre-registered as ten Tier-1 criteria with explicit thresholds: runs unattended 18 of 20 sessions; ZERO point-in-time failures; zero paper batches on a stale or future-dated panel; under 10% of batches lost to model refusal or malformed output; the risk gate rejecting for explicable reasons; no proposal escaping the gate that should not have; settlement complete and idempotent; at least 60% of sized decisions carrying news; theses reviewable; every halt explained. Failure in point-in-time, panel freshness, gate escape or settlement STOPS the run -- those are integrity failures, and continuing past them produces a record that means nothing. AND WHAT IT CANNOT: edge; whether news carries the edge (the newsSplit readout needs 20+ outcomes per arm and will correctly refuse to compare); behaviour in an unseen regime; and whether the 15% drawdown brake can coexist with a months-long turnaround thesis, which needs a thesis to run its course.
